D-49 (2026-09-04, user decision on O-37): the device-grant credential class MAY mutate. The command surface is extended to accept device-grant bearer authentication rather than building a separate native command API. Rationale: `require_trusted_origin` is a CSRF defence, and CSRF applies only to ambient cookie authentication -- a Bearer client is not exposed to it, so not requiring an Origin for bearer requests is standard practice rather than a weakening of the browser posture, which is untouched. Rejected alternative: a separate native command surface, because iPhone (Phase 4) and MCP (Phase 5) would inherit the same split and SRV-02 exists precisely to keep ONE set of semantic invariants across adapters. Rejected alternative: a pull-only Mac client, because tasks would never leave the Mac -- the Phase 2 backup infrastructure would keep protecting an empty database and the single local SQLite file would remain the only copy of the user's data. Scope: the device-grant pipeline gains the command routes, `packages/contracts/openapi/keepling.yaml` widens the DeviceBearer scope beyond the four read routes it declares today, and `current_account_id` must be derived from the grant, which currently assigns only `device_grant_namespace`. The five-field server-derived namespace authority is UNCHANGED and still server-derived.

(b) O-31(b) apps/web DEFERRED out of KPL-03: apps/web has no synchronization or connectivity concept at any layer -- no channel, no ClientFacade method, nothing to render -- so this is unbuilt product surface rather than a Mac gap, and MAC-04 is a Mac requirement. D-52 (2026-09-04, user decision on O-51): undo of a mutation the server never received DROPS it from the outbox and reverts locally; undo of an acknowledged mutation continues to use the server-issued handle. Rejected: (a) accepting 03-23 as shipped, which leaves Command-Z dead on an unconfigured Mac while MAC-01 promises undo; (b) folding O-51 into O-43, which is the larger product question of where refused intent lives and does not need to block this. Rationale: if the bytes never left the machine there is nothing to reconcile, so no divergence window exists. CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSAL AS PUT: this is NOT implementable as a simple predicate. The outbox is (mutation_id, sequence) only (migrations/0001_initial.sql:49-52) and carries no in-flight marker, so today it cannot distinguish never-transmitted from awaiting-acknowledgement; dropping the wrong row would let the server accept a command the client deleted -- the same divergence by another route. It therefore requires explicit outbox state (queued vs in_flight, entered before the POST and returned to queued on transport failure) and a schema migration, which additionally requires generalising the migration runner (local-store.ts:934-949 is hardcoded to version 1 with a checksum binding). Scoped as 03-24.

D-52 IMPLEMENTED (03-24), with one correction to the decision text itself: a transport failure returns an outbox row to `uncertain`, NOT to `queued` as D-52's scoping paragraph said. The two cannot both hold -- a failed fetch cannot say whether the bytes left -- and the plan's own prohibition (ambiguous state is a refusal, never an assumed `queued`) is the one that keeps the divergence window closed. The shipped vocabulary is therefore three states, not two: `queued` (never transmitted, the only droppable state), `in_flight` (handed over in this process), `uncertain` (handed over, no outcome known -- still pushed under the server's idempotency, never droppable). Transitions are monotonic: a row that leaves `queued` never returns.

Fixed by 03-18 (509e323), which converted A1 (enabled state, sync status), A2 (row announcements, roving focus, selection), A3 (both dialogs and the conflict heading), A5 (detail mount, Complete/Reopen, final focus), A6 (both dialog focus reads), A8 (settings pane, arbitration), A9 (caret before/after, frontmost return), A11 (selection, disabled state), A14 (the live re-theme now settles on legibility, not merely on the background having changed) and A15 (layout reflow after resize). A6's ad-hoc polling loop was folded into settledFocus, so the file has exactly two waiting mechanisms: settledFocus(handle, {until}) for AX focus and waitFor for everything else. No assertion was weakened; waitFor gained onTimeout:'return' so a deadline hands the last observation to the caller's own check instead of aborting the row with only a timeout. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the rule as previously stated here: the settle predicate must NOT be 'strictly weaker than the assertion' / 'wait for focus to stop moving'. Quiescence settles on the failure state, because an absent focus and a pending dead key are both stable indefinitely. The correct rule, now written into waitFor's own documentation in the lane, is: poll for the CONDITION YOU ARE ABOUT TO ASSERT, to a bounded deadline, and report the last observation if it never holds. That does not make a row vacuous -- a condition that never holds still fails. MEASURED after the fix: ten consecutive `--all` runs, 150/150 row executions passed, 92 cases each, all ten reporting SETTINGS restore=VERIFIED; runs 4 and 7 under full CPU load (18 spinners on 18 cores) took 222s and 208s against an idle 168-171s and still passed. See 03-18-SUMMARY.md.

open_items.item: CLOSED - the desktop 'offline' presentation state is real, constructed in production, and proven to reach a user
open_items.detail:
MAC-04 requires the user to inspect offline, syncing, conflict, authentication-expired and unrecoverable states. Mapped onto the real vocabulary in apps/desktop/main/application/presentation.ts these are offline / updating / conflict / authentication_required / store_unavailable. Four are genuinely published: updating at DesktopApplication.ts:446,449; authentication_required at main/index.ts:462; store_unavailable at DesktopApplication.ts:250,377; and per-task conflict is surfaced through the workspace conflict region in packages/web-ui (21 refs, covered by state-matrix.test.tsx). `{ kind: 'offline' }` is DECLARED in the DesktopPresentationInput union (presentation.ts:35), has authored copy ('Offline -- showing tasks saved on this Mac'), and is unit-tested at test/application/recovery-presentation.test.ts:23 -- but grep across apps/ packages/ tooling/ finds NO production construction anywhere. The sync pass settles only into healthy / local_saved / retryable_failure (DesktopApplication.ts:483,486). A user who unplugs the network therefore never sees the offline state; they see retryable_failure copy instead. This is the same shape as O-9/O-11/O-12/O-15/O-16/O-21: complete, tested, unreachable. It was NOT caught by the mechanical GAP-1 sweep, which looks for exported SYMBOLS referenced only by tests; this is a union VARIANT never constructed, which that sweep cannot see. Generalise the detector to state variants before trusting it as a clean bill of health.

CLOSED 2026-09-03 by 03-19. The discriminator lives in the transport, the only layer that knows whether bytes came back: KeeplingSyncAdapter#json wraps the fetch call alone and rethrows a tagged SyncUnreachableError (main/application/sync-reachability.ts), and runSyncPass() reads the tag -- it never sniffs message text. A server that ANSWERED badly (500, malformed body, bounded-page violation) still lands on retryable_failure. An app with no server configured makes no request at all and settles offline with a null contact, because healthy would read as 'everything is synchronized' and local_saved promises a sync nothing is arranged to perform. lastSuccessfulContact has a durable source: NodeSqliteLocalStore.recordSuccessfulContact writes the instant the server answered into namespace_metadata, it is routed through the store-worker protocol and forwarded by WorkerLocalStore, and syncState() reads it back across relaunches; it is null when the server has never answered. Proof is shipped-entry-point, not fixture: test/e2e/gap-closure.spec.ts launches the real dist/main/index.cjs with the real KeeplingSyncAdapter (KEEPLING_TEST_SYNC_MODE deliberately unset) against a closed loopback port, a real 500 server, and no server at all, and reads the row off the rendered window. Gate: lanes=9 failed=0. NOTE the generalisation in this item is NOT closed and is carried forward as O-33: the mechanical GAP-1 sweep still cannot see a union VARIANT that is never constructed.

open_items.item: Fixed deadlines in the macOS lane are tuned standalone but consumed in `--all`, which runs about 1.6x slower
open_items.detail: Measured by 03-19 on application_digest=e1c9d695da26507ae3a6a3b711f6884df5602022efe62d4a0b0cdf5b389754a4. A6's final case ('after discarding changes and navigating away') failed inside a full --all run with 'last read was nothing', while the SAME row passed 4/4 standalone. Row duration: 39.5s inside --all against 24.9-25.5s standalone. The preceding VoiceOver-layer rows leave an AX client attached and every focus change costs more under one. The specific race was a deadline asymmetry INSIDE A6 -- it waited 10s for a dialog to OPEN but only 5s for focus to be restored after one CLOSES, even though restoration is the slower operation (the destructive branch commits a route change, re-renders the list, and runs two focus effects). Fixed by making both 10s, which weakens nothing: usableFocus(last) is asserted exactly as before and settledFocus still returns whatever it last saw at the deadline, so genuinely lost focus still fails loudly. GENERALISE: every other fixed timeoutMs/sleep in tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs was chosen against standalone timings and is therefore under-budgeted in the context the gate actually runs it in. Audit them against --all timings rather than waiting for each to flake once. This does not invalidate O-29's bound; it names a mechanism the bound covers.
open_items.closed_detail: Closed by 03-20 by removing per-row deadline tuning entirely rather than auditing each deadline against --all timings. tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs now defines ONE lane-wide WAIT_SCALE that multiplies every bounded wait (waitFor, settledFocus, ensureFrontmost, the launch and teardown loops), applied UNIFORMLY rather than only under --all -- a mode-dependent factor would recreate the very standalone/--all split the item describes. Scaling weakens no assertion and costs nothing on the happy path: a wait whose condition is already true returns on its first poll, so the larger budget is spent only on a genuine failure. The generalisation clause is also satisfied: 31 non-polling sleep() calls were converted to wait on the observable consequence of the preceding action, leaving 9 sleeps, all inside polling loops or Promise.race deadlines, none preceding an action. MEASURED after the change on application_digest=937b279ce76952f0180c31ca1cf0deee0ccd42b199a13116d5f22adcfe3c2684: A3 took 11554-11924ms inside five consecutive --all runs against 11752-11894ms standalone -- the asymmetry the item names (29.5s vs 14.6-16.5s) is gone, not merely padded. Five consecutive --all runs at rows=15 failed=0 cases=92; gate lanes=9 failed=0.

Verified: no script in tooling/ or scripts/, no package.json target, no gate lane, and no commit in all of history that ever added such a file; `git grep "GAP-1"` matches only prose in .planning/ plus two test files. Every "sweep" in this phase was a human or agent running git grep by hand, once per symbol, recorded as prose in this file (see the O-12 closeout, which cites exactly that). CONSEQUENCE: no statement of the form "the GAP-1 sweep came back clean" in any plan, summary or commit in this repository is mechanical evidence, and none should ever be cited as if it were. That is why O-30 survived -- not a detector with a blind spot, but no detector. STILL OPEN, re-scoped: building a real reachability checker is net-new static analysis (enumerate union members from the AST, find object-literal construction sites in production files, diff the discriminant sets, and distinguish CONSTRUCTING a variant from merely switch-casing on it -- that last part is why regex cannot do it, since the consumer switch mentions every variant whether or not anything builds one). Low-to-mid hundreds of lines plus a gate lane. Deliberately NOT done in KPL-03: it would be the least-tested code in the repo at the moment of shipping. Note for whoever builds it: ts-morph@26 resolves today ONLY as a transitive dependency of shadcn surviving on hoisted node_modules (.npmrc node-linker=hoisted); declare it explicitly rather than relying on that.

open_items.item: CLOSED - the packaged Mac app is proven against real Phoenix on real PostgreSQL
open_items.detail:
BROADENED 2026-09-04. Filed originally as 'packaged tests use the stub'. The truth is larger and was found by verifying a citation instead of trusting it. apps/desktop/test/e2e/real-stack-sync.spec.ts, DESPITE ITS NAME, constructs KeeplingSyncAdapter with a stubbed `fetch` against the non-resolving host https://server.keepling.invalid (lines 35-36, 327-328, 497-498). Every spec in test/packaged/ sets KEEPLING_TEST_SYNC_MODE and so exercises the inline stub SyncPort. The only desktop test touching localhost is gap-closure.spec.ts, which stands up a bare 500-responding loopback server and a closed port to prove offline DETECTION -- not synchronization. So the Electron adapter has NEVER exchanged a byte with Phoenix.

Consequences: MAC-03's 'later reconcile' clause, MAC-05's 'not only a development renderer ... synchronizes' clause, and SRV-02's Electron adapter proof all rest on a fake. This is O-20's rule applied to the largest remaining subsystem: code that has only ever executed under fixtures is not proven code.

FEASIBLE, and cheaper than it looks: apps/web/e2e/support/stack.ts already spawns real PostgreSQL and Phoenix for the web lane, and the packaged specs already spread ...process.env so they can be pointed at a base URL. The work is wiring the desktop lane to that existing harness, not building a server story from scratch.

NOTE ON MY OWN ERROR: MAC-03 was checked on 2026-09-04 citing this spec as real-server proof, and unchecked hours later once the citation was actually read. A test named 'real-stack' that stubs its transport is exactly the kind of thing this ledger exists to catch, and the name did the deceiving.

PARTIALLY ADVANCED 2026-09-04 by 03-21, then BLOCKED on O-37. The shared harness half is done and committed (772ea1a): the real PostgreSQL + migrations + seed + Phoenix half of apps/web/e2e/support/stack.ts was EXTRACTED to apps/web/e2e/support/backend.ts and is now imported by stack.ts, so a desktop lane can reuse the exact harness the web lane proves against instead of a second drifting copy. The environment caveat recorded elsewhere in this handoff does NOT apply here: PostgreSQL 18.6 starts cleanly on this machine, there is no shmget failure, and the refactored stack was observed reaching 'Keepling Playwright stack ready at http://127.0.0.1:4173' with real Phoenix.

The lane itself is blocked, and by something larger than tooling. Probed directly against that running real server with a real device grant obtained through the real /oauth/authorize -> code -> PKCE /oauth/token path (token 200, five-field server-derived namespace origin=http://localhost:4002 issuer=http://localhost:4002 server_instance=local-test generation=1 account_subject=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001): GET /api/v1/sync returns 200 for the device bearer, but POST /api/v1/commands/capture-task and GET /api/v1/mutations/{id} both return 401 authentication_required for the SAME bearer. See O-37. Until that is decided, the packaged app can authorize and pull against real Phoenix but structurally cannot push, so the must_have 'reaches Synced only on an exact receipt' is unreachable against a real server and no honest lane can assert it.

CLOSED 2026-09-04 by 03-21. apps/desktop/test/real-stack/real-stack-sync.spec.ts launches the PACKAGED .app from the manifest with KEEPLING_TEST_SYNC_MODE deliberately unset, so the real KeeplingSyncAdapter runs, against real Phoenix on real PostgreSQL started by the SHARED harness apps/web/e2e/support/backend.ts (extracted from the web lane's stack.ts and imported, never copied). It authorizes through the real device-grant path (the app builds the URL and hands it to shell.openExternal; the test plays only the system-browser half, driving the real /oauth/authorize and feeding the real keepling://auth/callback back through the app's own open-url handler), captures while the server is unreachable, proves the SERVER itself has no such mutation (404, not merely "the client did not say Synced"), reconnects, and reaches Synced. The exact serialized bytes are checked against what the server RECEIVED, recorded by the forwarding proxy, not against the client's own claim; the receipt matches mutation identity and task identity; and both titles are read back out of real PostgreSQL through the server's own /api/v1/inbox.

OUTCOMES OBSERVED: "accepted" only. The lane deliberately does not construct a conflict or rejection -- see O-38. It does NOT prove conflict reconciliation and does not claim to.

NON-VACUITY, measured rather than asserted: the lane failed four times during construction for four genuinely different real reasons (PostgreSQL's 103-byte Unix-socket path limit, the packaged app sending a command body with no "version", a stale Settings pane, and a real race in handleCallback), and a deliberate mutation -- pointing the app at a port with nothing listening -- makes it FAIL. The spec was restored byte-identically afterwards. tooling/verify-real-stack-desktop.mjs additionally refuses the lane if KEEPLING_TEST_SYNC_MODE appears in the spec or the environment, if a stubbed fetch or a .invalid host appears, if the shared harness import disappears, or if the spec does not print a REAL_STACK_SYNC line carrying a positive settled count and a proven exact-bytes retry.

THREE REAL CLIENT/SERVER DISAGREEMENTS fell out of the first run and are all fixed: the device grant could not mutate at all (O-37/D-49); the desktop's durable command bytes omitted the contract-required "version" and so would have been refused 400 by any real server; and the client kind was recorded as "web".

DISPOSITION OF THE MISLEADING NAME: test/e2e/real-stack-sync.spec.ts is RENAMED to test/e2e/fixture-server-sync.spec.ts and KEPT. It never had a real stack, and its name alone got MAC-03 checked on a false citation. It is kept because what it actually does is valuable and is NOT covered by the real lane -- PKCE state matching, an unsolicited callback from a competing app, single-use codes, refresh rotation, detected refresh replay, sign-out fencing order, and a hostile server answering with someone else's mutation identity, several of which cannot be induced against an honest real server. The D-48 ownership registry follows the rename and gains a "real-server" category.

open_items.item: CLOSED - Quick Entry focus restoration and window-level Escape binding
open_items.detail:
MEASURED directly on application_digest=937b279ce76952f0180c31ca1cf0deee0ccd42b199a13116d5f22adcfe3c2684 with a standalone AXProbe diagnostic, twice, deterministically. Sequence: open Quick Entry by the real global accelerator, type a draft, tab to "Discard Draft...", Space, then Space on "Keep Draft". Observed focus after the dialog closes: AXWebArea "Keepling" -- the DOCUMENT, not the "Discard Draft..." button that opened the dialog. apps/desktop/renderer/quick-entry.tsx binds its Escape handler with onKeyDown on a div INSIDE the React root, so a keydown targeted at the document never reaches it: Escape was posted and BOTH windows were still present 2s later (windows=["Keepling","Keepling - Inbox"], capture fields=2). Tabbing back into the capture field first and posting the SAME Escape hid the window immediately (windows=["Keepling - Inbox"], capture fields=1). So a person who opens the discard confirmation and keeps their draft loses Escape as a way out of Quick Entry until they tab somewhere. WHY A6 DOES NOT CATCH IT: usableFocus() accepts any non-AXApplication node with a non-zero frame, and the AXWebArea qualifies -- focus is 'usable' but is not on the invoking control, which is what WAI-ARIA requires of a dismissed dialog. Tightening usableFocus to exclude AXWebArea/AXGroup container roles would turn this into a red row; that is a deliberate decision for a later plan, not a silent change. 03-20 did NOT work around it silently: A3 and A6 use Escape there only as teardown and now call returnFocusIntoQuickEntry() first, with the finding named in the helper's comment. Compare Keep Editing in the workspace unsaved-changes dialog, which restores focus correctly -- so this is specific to the Quick Entry alertdialog, and the fix is a ref-based restore in quick-entry.tsx.

CLOSED 2026-09-04 by 03-21 (302f13e), with BOTH defects fixed rather than only the visible one. (1) The discard confirmation now returns focus to the control that OPENED it when that control still exists (Keep Draft), and to the title field when it does not (Discard Draft unmounts 'Discard Draft...' along with the draft, so the fallback is the live path on the confirm branch, not decoration). (2) Escape and Command-Return moved from '<div onKeyDown>' to a WINDOW-level keydown listener, held through a ref so it registers once and still sees the current draft and submission state. That makes the guarantee structural: there is no focus position inside the Quick Entry window from which Escape can fail, so the next dialog that returns focus to nowhere cannot re-arm this trap. Deliberately NOT a main-process global accelerator -- Escape is a window-local key and a global one would swallow Escape from every other application on this Mac. RED first: both new @windowed tests in test/e2e/keyboard-quick-entry.spec.ts failed before the change (the second timed out with the window still open, which is the defect verbatim); 7/7 pass after, with no existing assertion weakened. macOS rows A3 5/5 and A6 6/6 PASS. usableFocus() in tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs still ACCEPTS the AXWebArea and is deliberately left alone -- tightening it is a real follow-up (it is what made A6 blind here) but would turn unrelated rows red, so it is carried as its own decision and not smuggled into this fix.

open_items.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by 03-21 while building the O-34 real-stack lane, by doing exactly what O-34 asked: pointing a real client at a real server. It is a product defect, not a test problem, and it was invisible for as long as every desktop test faked its transport.

MEASURED against real Phoenix (MIX_ENV=test) on real PostgreSQL 18.6, using a device grant obtained through the REAL browser-delegated path (POST /api/v1/test/session for the browser half, then GET /oauth/authorize -> 302 keepling://auth/callback?code&state -> POST /oauth/token with the PKCE verifier -> 200 with the five server-derived namespace fields):
  GET  /api/v1/sync                     -> 200  (device bearer accepted)
  POST /api/v1/commands/capture-task    -> 401 authentication_required
  GET  /api/v1/mutations/{mutation_id}  -> 401 authentication_required
Same bearer, same connection, same second.

CAUSE, in the router: the :device_grant_authenticated pipeline (KeeplingWeb.Auth#authenticate_device_grant) covers only /api/v1/device-grants*, /api/v1/sync and /api/v1/sync/bootstrap. Every /api/v1/commands/* route and GET /api/v1/mutations/:id sit behind [:api, :authenticated, :mutation], which requires a BROWSER SESSION COOKIE and, through :mutation -> require_trusted_origin, an Origin header matching the request host. KeeplingSyncAdapter sends a Bearer token and no cookie and no Origin, by design. The published contract agrees with the server, not with the client: packages/contracts/openapi/keepling.yaml declares the DeviceBearer security scheme on /device-grants* and /sync* only, and declares no security at all on /commands/* or /mutations/{id}.

CONSEQUENCE: the shipped Mac app can authorize, bind its namespace, and pull, but it can never push. DesktopApplication.runSyncPass throws on the first push, settles retryable_failure, and the outbox correctly keeps the exact serialized bytes forever. Nothing is lost and nothing lies -- 'Saved on this Mac' stays truthful -- but 'Synced' is unreachable against a real server, and MAC-03 / MAC-05 / SRV-02's Electron adapter proof cannot be honestly completed until this is resolved.

WHY THIS STOPPED RATHER THAN BEING AUTO-FIXED (deviation Rule 4): the fix decides WHICH CREDENTIAL CLASS MAY MUTATE DATA. It changes a published contract with its own gate (contracts:check), it changes the server's authentication surface for the entire command API, it requires deciding whether require_trusted_origin -- a browser CSRF defence -- applies to a non-browser client or must be replaced by something else for it, and it requires new authorization plumbing to derive the account context the command controllers read (conn.assigns.current_account_id) from a device grant, which today assigns only current_device_grant_id and device_grant_namespace. None of those files are in 03-21's scope, and REQUIREMENTS.md deliberately phases SRV-02 across adapters, so 'which adapters may mutate' is a live design question rather than an oversight to paper over.

OPTIONS FOR THE DECIDER (not ranked -- this is the decision):
  A. Extend the device-grant pipeline to the command surface and the mutation lookup, update the OpenAPI security declarations to match, derive account context from the grant, and state explicitly what replaces require_trusted_origin for a bearer client.
  B. Add a distinct native command surface (e.g. /api/v1/native/commands/*) so the browser surface's CSRF posture is untouched, and point KeeplingSyncAdapter at it.
  C. Accept it for this milestone: record that the Mac app is pull-only against a real server, land the real-stack lane asserting exactly that (authorize + pull real, push refused, never Synced, exact bytes retained), and move the push proof to the phase that owns it.
Option C is the only one that needs no server change, and it is honest, but it means MAC-03/MAC-05 stay unchecked with a stated reason rather than becoming checkable in Phase 3.

CLOSED 2026-09-04 by 03-21 under D-49 (option A). ONE credential decision now lives in KeeplingWeb.Auth#authenticate_client: a request presenting Authorization: Bearer is a native client, authenticated by its device grant, with CSRF checks skipped because there is no ambient credential to ride; every other request is a browser and takes exactly the path it took before -- load_session, require_authenticated, protect_from_forgery, then require_trusted_origin for mutations -- with nothing removed and nothing made conditional. The browser posture is PINNED by tests rather than asserted in prose: a cookie-authenticated POST with no Origin and with a foreign Origin are both still 403 origin_not_allowed, and those two assertions passed BEFORE the change and still pass after. current_account_id and current_client_kind are derived from the grant and from nowhere else, so a native client cannot write outside the namespace its credential is bound to; client_kind was hardcoded "web", which would have recorded a Mac capture as a browser capture in the user's own activity feed. The receipt read (GET /api/v1/mutations/:id) moved with the write, because a client that may issue a mutation must be able to read its stored result or the write is unsettleable after a dropped connection. Session-management routes (reauthenticate, logout, sessions) deliberately stayed browser-only. Contract updated and regenerated: DeviceBearer plus a newly declared BrowserSession scheme on the 19 command routes and the mutation lookup; contracts:check green. Eleven server tests, hostile cases included (revoked grant, expired credential, a session credential presented as a Bearer, and a body attempting to assert any of the five namespace fields). Server suite 188 passed; production routes still expose no test-only control.

open_items.item: Settings shows a stale account state after the browser sign-in callback lands
open_items.detail: FOUND 2026-09-04 by 03-21 while building the real-stack lane. apps/desktop/renderer/settings.tsx reads account status on mount and after its OWN actions (submitConnect, disconnect). Nothing pushes a change into it when the keepling://auth/callback is applied in the main process, so after a successful browser sign-in the pane keeps saying "Finish signing in with Keepling in your browser." until it is re-read. The sign-in itself is completely successful -- credential stored, namespace bound, sync pass run -- so this is a staleness defect in one pane, not an authentication defect. The real-stack lane works around it by RELOADING the Settings renderer, which is a read and not a nudge, and says so in a comment at the call site. The fix is a subscription or an invalidation on the channel that already carries presentation updates; deliberately not done in 03-21, which had no renderer scope beyond Quick Entry.

open_items.item: The packaged application digest is not reproducible across invocations at the same revision, which the macOS evidence-reuse idiom depends on
open_items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 during 03-21. At one unchanged revision (fc3ac82, clean tree) `pnpm package:desktop` produced THREE different applicationDigestSha256 values across separate invocations (87c7279a..., 1d79a643..., 6bc3dd8a...), while two back-to-back invocations in a single shell produced identical digests. Nothing test-related is inside the bundle -- app.asar contains no spec or Playwright files -- so the variation is in the build/forge/ad-hoc-signing output rather than in the source set.

WHY IT MATTERS: tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs binds recorded evidence to the exact application digest, and tooling/verify-desktop-phase.mjs re-packages in its own package-once lane before reusing that evidence. When the digest drifts, macos-integration fails with "no macOS integration evidence exists for application digest ..." and the 160-second row suite must be re-run -- which happened twice in this session. The binding is CORRECT and must not be weakened; the packaging is what should be made reproducible. Do NOT respond to this by loosening the digest check: that binding is the only thing stopping one lucky row run from becoming durable green.

WORKAROUND until fixed: run `pnpm package:desktop && node tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs --all`, then the gate, and re-record if the gate reports a digest mismatch.

open_items.item: The real adapter throws on the conflict and rejected outcomes the server emits and the contract publishes; { kind: 'conflict' } has no production construction site
open_items.detail:
FILED 2026-09-04 by the coordinator from a hand-audit of the DesktopPresentationInput / SyncOutcome unions, and MIRRORED here into open_items by 03-21 because O-22 is precisely the habit of recording an item only in prose and then having it read as closed. The authoritative text is the MAC-04 note in .planning/REQUIREMENTS.md; this entry exists so the item is visible to anything that reads open_items.

SUBSTANCE: apps/desktop/main/adapters/sync.ts:90-94 mapAcknowledgement accepts ONLY "accepted" and "already_satisfied" and throws "server acknowledgement is invalid" on anything else, while packages/contracts/openapi/keepling.yaml declares "conflict" and "rejected" in the outcome enum and apps/server command_store.ex:707 genuinely persists conflicts. The union variant { kind: 'conflict' } in presentation.ts has authored copy, a Review Conflict action and a unit-test fixture, and no production construction site anywhere -- the same shape as O-30, which is what O-33 was supposed to generalise. MAC-04 is un-checked over it.

WHY IT IS LIVE NOW: this was latent only because no packaged path had ever reached a real server. Closing O-37/O-34 makes it reachable.

EXPLICITLY NOT 03-21's: the 03-21 real-stack lane was directed to exercise the ACCEPTED path only and does so, observing outcome "accepted" and nothing else. It does not construct a conflict or rejection, and it did not widen mapAcknowledgement, catch the throw, or otherwise make the validator more permissive -- doing that without also building the conflict presentation path would convert a loud failure into a silent one. Owned by 03-22.
open_items.resolution: CLOSED by 03-22, BOTH halves. CORRECTION to the filed text: CommandAcknowledgement.outcome publishes exactly accepted/already_satisfied, so a 200 claiming conflict IS invalid and mapAcknowledgement is right to refuse it; conflict/rejected at keepling.yaml:1392 are MutationTrustState, a CLIENT vocabulary. The real server answers a conflict with HTTP 409 + an RFC 9457 problem and a semantic refusal with 422. So the defect was worse than filed: adapters/sync.ts#json threw a plain Error for every non-OK status, runSyncPass caught it, and a 409 landed on "Couldn t reach the server" with a Retry that would retry a decided command forever -- MISHEARD as a transport failure. (a) main/adapters/server-refusal.ts classifies a CLOSED list (four 409 conflict codes, every 422, invalid_command, task_not_found); a 401 is tagged separately and is NEVER collapsed into a per-mutation rejection, because every authentication problem carries retryable:false; 403/5xx/malformed still throw. mapAcknowledgement was NOT widened. (b) { kind: conflict }, { kind: rejected } and { kind: authentication_required } are constructed in runSyncPass and reach the shipped window with their authored copy and action.

open_items.item: Only capture_task can ever reach the server -- edits, lifecycle and Today moves mutate the local projection and enqueue NOTHING
open_items.detail: Reported by 03-21 and verified independently 2026-09-04: `type: capture_task` at main/application/DesktopApplication.ts:259 is the ONLY command type constructed anywhere in desktop production code, and store-worker/local-store.ts:697 guards on it. editTask (DesktopApplication.ts:295), applyLifecycle (:307) and moveToday (:314) each write the local store and return a WorkspaceSnapshot without enqueuing an outbound command; there is not a single production `enqueue` call site in main/, store-worker/ or renderer/. Consequence for MAC-03: the requirement says `mutate tasks ... and later reconcile`, and only CAPTURES reconcile. Completing, reopening, trashing, restoring, editing a title or moving to Today are durable on this Mac and invisible to the server forever. This is NOT a regression and NOT a defect introduced by 03-21 -- it is the sync seam having only ever been built for one command type, which stayed invisible while no packaged path reached a real server at all (O-34). It is the same family as O-37 and O-38: the client and the contract disagree about what the client can do. The server accepts the other command types (packages/contracts/openapi/keepling.yaml command enum) -- nothing on the wire needs to change. Do NOT close MAC-03 by narrowing it to captures without a recorded decision.

open_items.item: A locally refused change has no durable home: the next pull reverts it, while the copy says "Your version is still on this Mac."
open_items.detail: FILED 2026-09-04 by 03-22 while closing O-38. store-worker/local-store.ts#acknowledge no longer replays the canonical shadow after a conflict or rejection, which is what keeps the person edit on screen immediately after a refusal and makes the authored copy true at that moment. But the refused command is TERMINAL and is deleted from the outbox (leaving it queued would retry the same immutable bytes forever against a server that has already decided), so the visible projection -- a replay of (canonical shadow + outbox) -- no longer contains it anywhere. The NEXT applyPull replays the shadow and the local value is lost. Giving a refused local change a durable home (a quarantine table? a re-editable draft? MutationTrustState publishes "quarantined") is a product decision 03-22 had no authority to make. Do NOT resolve this by keeping refused commands in the outbox.

open_items.item: The desktop conflict chooser is title-only, so a lifecycle or Trash conflict gets copy and a refresh but no mine/current choice
open_items.detail: FILED 2026-09-04 by 03-22. packages/web-ui/src/tasks/ConflictResolver.tsx asks which TITLE to keep, and WorkspaceConflictView.field is the literal type "title". A server task_lifecycle_conflict/task_trash_conflict diverges on completed_at/trashed_at, and offering two ISO timestamps under that wording would be a lie in the UI, so local-store.ts records a mine/current conflict row ONLY when the server named a divergent title. Those conflicts still reach a person as the { kind: conflict } row and its live Review Conflict action, which falls back to running a pass -- exactly the refresh_task recovery the server itself names for them. apps/web ALREADY has the multi-field resolver (apps/web/src/features/tasks/ConflictResolver.tsx, "Use mine for {label}"); the desktop does not. Closing this is porting that resolver and widening ConflictRecord/resolveConflict to apply a choice to the right column.

open_items.item: CLOSED - undo reconciles: a server-issued handle is retained, an offline undo survives relaunch and reverses the change on the real server, and an undo with no handle is refused out loud
open_items.detail: CLOSED 2026-09-04 by 03-23. The handle is retained from CommandAcknowledgement.undo (UndoAvailability: expires_at, handle, label), never minted or derived; a malformed one throws rather than being repaired. The command is exactly UndoTaskCommand -- handle, mutation_id, version, plus the optional type discriminator, NO task_id and NO expected_revision, because the server resolves both from the handle it minted and decode_undo compares the key set exactly. Ordering is 03-22's task:<id> resource key, not a second mechanism. The projection revert and the outbox insert share one transaction. Handles live in namespace_metadata rather than a new table because there is exactly one migration and #applyMigration would fault every existing local store into migration_checksum_drift. THE PLAN'S PROSE WAS WRONG about where the expiry lives and the contract won: POST /commands/undo-task publishes UndoResult, a oneOf of CommandAcknowledgement and UndoNoChange, and the server answers a no-change with HTTP 200 (404 only for unknown), so adding undo_expired to REJECTION_CODES alone would have changed nothing -- classifyServerRefusal was only ever reached for a non-OK status. It is still ONE closed list, now also consulted at 200/404. Before the fix a 200 no-change had no snapshot, mapAcknowledgement threw, and a decided undo landed on 'Couldn't reach the server' with a Retry button that would retry it forever -- the O-38 misdiagnosis one endpoint later. undo_uncertain is deliberately NEVER settled (the server itself does not know), which leaves O-47 untouched. VERIFIED BY: node tooling/verify-desktop-phase.mjs -> lanes=10 failed=0, real-stack-sync lane printing REAL_STACK_UNDO handle=server_issued undo_arrived=1 reverted_on_server=1 survived_relaunch=1 refused_without_handle=1 on application_digest=2783671b10fd4ce386ca77dc4c9730ba7c4bed568eeee5e2c8fd27f7da8a349e. Evidence is the SERVER's own completed_at returning to null and the exact bytes recorded arriving at /commands/undo-task by the forwarding proxy -- never the client's 'Synced' label. Reasoning and what was NOT observed (a real expired handle, a real undo_uncertain) in 03-23-SUMMARY.md.

open_items.item: { kind: uncertain } and its Check Again action still have no production construction site -- reported for a recorded decision
open_items.detail:
REPORTED 2026-09-04 by 03-22, as its plan directed. "Checking whether this change was accepted..." with a Check Again action is the IN-DOUBT state: a push whose answer never arrived, where the mutation may or may not have been accepted. Today every unanswered request lands on { kind: offline } (SyncUnreachableError), because the transport cannot distinguish "the request never left" from "it left and the answer was lost" -- fetch rejecting covers both. Constructing uncertain honestly requires the transport to report whether the request body was flushed. The RESOLUTION already exists: KeeplingSyncAdapter.lookup(mutationId, fingerprint) re-reads the exact stored receipt and is already wired for reconcile(), so Check Again has somewhere real to go the moment the state can be entered. SyncStatusRow already handles the check_again code, so no dead button is created by leaving this unconstructed. Do NOT delete the variant.

STILL OPEN after 03-24, and named explicitly rather than wired silently. 03-24 introduced a DURABLE outbox state it calls `uncertain` -- the fact that a command's bytes were handed to the transport and no answer came back. That is adjacent to, but not the same as, the PRESENTATION variant `{ kind: 'uncertain' }`, which is a claim to a person about a specific change with a Check Again action. The variant remains unconstructed and this decision remains open. 03-24 also confirmed the blocker from the other side: a connection REFUSED provably transmitted nothing, but the adapter reports it identically to a socket error after the body was flushed, so undo refuses both. Refusing is safe and no correctness claim depends on narrowing it; narrowing it is this item's transport work.

open_items.item: CLOSED - undo is available again on a Mac with no server configured, without a divergence window
open_items.detail:
CLOSED 2026-09-04 by plan 03-24 under D-52 (commits 3d94f8e, c8a76df, 531f89e, d9e7df5, 616fec0, f7ab3c9, 548054c, 03d5744, aace10e). Not closed by the predicate the proposal assumed -- 'if it is still in the outbox, drop it' is WRONG, because a row sits in the outbox unchanged while its POST is in flight. migrations/0002_outbox_state.sql adds explicit transmission state (queued | in_flight | uncertain), applied by a migration runner generalised from its hardcoded version 1 while keeping the D-37 checksum binding per version. Undo drops a command ONLY when its state is `queued` and no later queued command shares its resource key; every other answer is a refusal.

CORRECTION TO THE PLAN AS WRITTEN, reported rather than silently resolved: the plan's design guidance said a transport failure returns a row to `queued`, and its own prohibition said absent or ambiguous state is a REFUSAL and never an assumed `queued`. Those contradict. A failed fetch cannot distinguish 'the request never left' from 'it left and the answer was lost' (that is O-47's own finding), so returning it to a droppable state would reopen the divergence by another route. The prohibition governs: a transport failure yields `uncertain`, which is still pushed and never droppable. The transitions are monotonic -- a row that leaves `queued` never returns -- and that is what makes the drop provably safe. For the same reason an `in_flight` row found at startup is PROMOTED to `uncertain`, never reset, and rows that predate the column migrate to `uncertain` rather than to the column default.

VERIFIED at 03-24 by `node tooling/verify-desktop-phase.mjs` -> lanes=10 failed=0 (typecheck-desktop 1, typecheck-web 1, unit 297, ipc 75, electron-e2e 66, package-once 1, packaged 11, real-stack-sync 5, macos-integration 93, privacy 1). The dangerous case is proved against real Phoenix rather than by asserting a branch: the forwarding proxy holds the ANSWER while the real bytes reach the real server, and `REAL_STACK_IN_FLIGHT held=1 refused=1 command_survived=1 server_holds_completion=1` records that an undo racing an in-flight command was refused, the command survived intact, and the server ended up holding the change -- so a drop would have deleted something the server accepted. `REAL_STACK_UNDO ... dropped_never_transmitted=1 never_reached_server=1` records the other half: a command that was provably never transmitted is dropped, and the server never receives it once the network returns. MAC-01's promise is proved on real macOS by row A5 (packaged app, no server, real CGEvent keystrokes), re-recorded at applicationDigestSha256=8058ed13b8b4d96897e159b369e771e8ff654313765b82772ad931eff9e5a3d3.

open_items.item: An undo refusal the store classifies as `unknown` shows copy claiming the change has not reached the server, which is untrue for a command the server already settled
open_items.detail: FILED 2026-09-04 by 03-24. `undoUnsentLocalAction` returns `unknown` when the recorded last action has no outbox row -- most often because the server SETTLED that command and issued no compensation capability (a `capture_task`, for instance, which is not in `Undo.@supported_commands`). The application maps that to `{ kind: 'undo_unavailable', reason: 'unsent' }`, whose copy is "This change hasn't reached the server yet, so it can't be undone." -- and it HAS reached the server. This is unchanged shipped behaviour from 03-23, not a regression introduced here; 03-24 left it alone deliberately rather than widening its scope into a copy decision. The honest answer is probably the `expired` copy ("This change can no longer be undone.") with no action offered, since no capability exists and syncing cannot produce one -- but that is a wording decision with a dead-remedy dimension (O-42), so it wants authority rather than an executor. SHAPE: identical to the A3 defect 03-20 fixed -- a row that passes alone and fails under --all because a PRIOR row left machine state behind. Prime suspect is A8, the immediately preceding row and the only one that registers a rival application-level global shortcut and forces real OS arbitration (ARBITRATION rival_registered=true keepling_claims_shortcut=true). The failure text is the O-36 signature (focus resolving to nothing), so check whether A8 leaves a rival application frontmost or holding the shortcut. FIX THE RACE IN A9. Do NOT re-run --all until it happens to pass and record that: O-29 exists precisely to forbid that move, and --all is the RECORDING path, so a lucky run becomes durable gate evidence.

open_items.item: READING TRAP: a green phase gate does NOT mean the macOS rows pass today -- that lane reuses recorded evidence and never re-runs the rows
open_items.detail: Recorded 2026-09-04 because the orchestrator (me) quoted `lanes=10 failed=0` as authoritative for the macOS rows repeatedly across this phase, and for that one lane it is not. Nine of the ten gate lanes execute their tests on every invocation. The macos-integration lane does NOT: it reuses evidence recorded by an earlier `--all` run, bound to applicationDigestSha256 plus the executable digest plus three Swift probe source digests plus laneSourceDigest. That binding is CORRECT and must never be loosened -- it is what makes stale evidence impossible and it demonstrably works (03-18 proved appending one comment to the lane makes the gate refuse the evidence). But its consequence is easy to misread: the lane reports PASS cases=92/93 by consulting a file, so it proves the rows passed WHEN RECORDED for this exact artifact, not that they pass now. O-55 is the live demonstration -- the gate was green on evidence 8058ed13 while a fresh --all run of the same artifact failed at A9. WHEN THIS MATTERS: any claim of the form "the macOS rows pass" needs a fresh `--all`, not a gate run. WHEN IT DOES NOT: promotion and digest-binding claims, which are exactly what the recorded evidence is for. Related: O-29 (flake bounded, not zero) and O-40 (the digest drifts across invocations, forcing re-records).
